validator: draft 1: hard problems on three sources (numbered from research.json, not from the prompt's own list) and a soft one on length (whatAmILookingAt 17144 characters). The faults below are the critic's.
keep: The idea is named in the first two sentences: legend, sources, state, then one path at a time, and then the question the job asks, what stops and what still runs.
Each step has its reason: conventions differ between sheets (legend), a sheet need not start at the top (sources), a drawn generator may be stopped (state), one part acts on several paths (trace).

Both of the brief's named misconceptions fail on screen: reading in reading order (screen 4, the board drawn with its supplies at the bottom, and the ringing of what you missed after every what-if) and not checking the sheet against the plant (screen 14, the last puzzle, HSG253's question).

The four new systems are all there (compressed air, a second switchboard, a hoist's control schematic, a bracket drawing), and the first switchboard comes back for the course's own puzzle on screen 13.

Typed only where the answer is a figure: the count of sources (2) and the upright's height (50 mm), each with its slips. Everything else is a named part, a set of valves or what stops, so it stays as choices.
Fourteen screens, opening on a puzzle he can feel his way through (the receiver), alternating show and do, ending on three mixed puzzles drawn from three different kinds of sheet.
The analogy is from his own trade (a periodic inspection of an unfamiliar installation) and says where it breaks: a sheet cannot show a change made after it was drawn.
fix: Sources: the [^n] numbers and quotes must be the prompt's list ([14] gate and globe, [4] EECO top of the page, [3] NAVEDTRA normal or neutral, [13] HSG253), copied exactly. The draft looked them up by research.json's own numbering.

Causal step skipped in the explain's state paragraph: it says a stopped generator feeds nothing, but not what that does to a line drawn joined to it. Add that the line is live only if another path joins it to a running source, which is the whole of screen 7.
False absolute: 'Layout never changes what is joined to what' in screen 14's why is true but reads as a slogan; say where a part sits does not change what it is joined to.

Overclaim in the explain: 'A source is anywhere supply can come in: a generator, ..., a pump or a compressor'. A pump is a source of flow on a piping sheet, not of supply on a board; say 'on a piping or air sheet, a pump or a compressor'.
Screen 9's hint 'in series with coil -K11' uses 'in series' where 'on the same path as' says it in his words and matches the trace step; he knows series, but the point is the path.
Screen 12's why says R1 'has a way in from each compressor', but the compressor lines join before R1. Say the joined line from the compressors comes in through V1 and V2.

Length: whatAmILookingAt is about 5000 characters over the soft limit. Cut the repeated rule sentences, the first switchboard's full description (only what screen 13 needs), the faint-and-bold contact detail already set by the hoist rule, and the after-Check sentences that repeat the why.
SHOW screen 10 runs to three sentences plus two instructions; make the instruction one tap ('Tap Trace') and keep the title block in the read line.
